full_judgment: 11. Mr. Nizamuddin Ryder has next contended that Rule 59 does not provide that for want of deposit or wrong deposit an election petition shall be dismissed. He has tried to draw an analogy between deposits made in pre-emption eases under the Bengal Tenancy Act, 1885 and the State Acquisition Act, 1950 and the deposits made under the Election Rules. He has argued that in the former there are specific provisions for dismissal of pre-emption cases in absence of deposits. This analogy, we find, is not applicable in Election cases simply because the deposits in pre-emption-cases are required for setting aside sales of land for transfer of the same to the pre-emptor.
